label: TP
reason: User-supplied header name flows directly into bar via doSomething, which returns it unchanged. The returned value is then converted to bytes and passed to encodeForHTML, whose output is concatenated into the HTTP response stream. There is no filtering or sanitization on the header name before it reaches the HTML encoder. Although ESAPI encoder is used, it operates on the encoded ciphertext derived from the input, not on the original unencoded user string itself, allowing potential XSS if the attacker controls the header name and influences the resulting plaintext or metadata exposure context.

evidence.note: header name flows to bar -> doSomething returns bar -> encoded and written to response
